findings.title: Exit code 4 silently reassigned, breaking scripts that check for recreate upgrade
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3; the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes the previous value of 4. Any consumer that was scripting against `update-compatibility check` and matching exit code 4 to detect a recreate-upgrade outcome will now silently treat a 'feature disabled' failure as a recreate upgrade. The error messages differ but the exit code, which is what the docs recommend scripts rely on ('they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command'), has changed. Even for a preview feature this is a contract break worth calling out in the release notes; alternatively, reserve a new code (e.g., 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED and leave RECREATE at 4 to preserve backward compatibility.

findings.title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
findings.body: The exit-code table describes code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.', but in this case the command does not actually determine whether a rolling upgrade is possible — `AbstractUpdatesCommand.printFeatureDisabled()` short-circuits the command and prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' before any compatibility analysis. The wording should make it clear that the command itself could not run (e.g., 'The command cannot run. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.') rather than implying a compatibility verdict was reached.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
findings.body: The test only verifies the stderr error message produced by `printFeatureDisabled()`, but the contract introduced by this PR is also that the command exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). The PR description and the docs explicitly state 'they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command', so the test for the new exit code should assert `cliResult.exitCode() == 4` (and ideally `assertExitCode`-style). Without it, an implementation that returned exit code 0 (or any other value) while still printing the message would not be caught.

findings.title: No coverage for UpdateCompatibilityCheck with feature disabled
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises `update-compatibility metadata` when the feature is disabled. `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` has the same feature gate added (see quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java) and is the more important subcommand for users (per docs: 'they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command'). A symmetric test launching `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates` and asserting both the error message and exit code 4 is needed to prevent regressions in the check subcommand.
